title: Check Receipts for the Missing Third Leg
scenario: It is 10:20 AM. The receipt log is proof that goods actually arrived - the third leg of the three-way match. Four of the five invoices have a matching receipt; one does not. Inspect the log and see why a missing receipt turns a three-way match into a two-way one.
input: PO-7742: 500 received, accepted, day-1. PO-7751: 300 received, accepted, day-1. PO-7738: 400 received, accepted, day-0. PO-7760: 200 received, accepted, day-1. PO-7763: NO receipt posted yet - the goods for INV-59005 have not been recorded as delivered.
instructions: Read the receipt log as proof of delivery, owned by the Receiving Desk.
Match each invoice's PO to a receipt.
Identify the invoice (INV-59005 / PO-7763) with no receipt and what that blocks.
Answer the questions and validate to mint the source profile.

questions.prompt: What does a goods receipt prove that a PO and an invoice do not?

options.text: That the goods actually arrived and were accepted
That the vendor is on file

questions.explain: A PO is the order and the invoice is the bill; only the receipt proves delivery. That is why it is the independent third leg of the match - it confirms Beacon actually got what it is being billed for.

questions.prompt: PO-7763 has no receipt. What does that make INV-59005's match?

options.text: A full three-way match - the receipt is optional
A two-way match only - invoice and PO agree, but delivery is unproven
An automatic pass, since price is within tolerance

questions.explain: With no receipt you can compare invoice to PO (two legs) but cannot confirm the goods arrived. That is a two-way match, and it is not enough to auto-approve a payment.

questions.prompt: INV-59005's price is within tolerance. Should it auto-approve despite the missing receipt?

options.text: Yes - a good price is enough
No - paying before delivery is confirmed risks paying for goods that never arrived
Yes - Receiving can post the receipt later

questions.explain: Price being fine does not prove delivery happened. Auto-approving a two-way match would let Beacon pay for undelivered goods, so the invoice is held until a receipt is posted.

questions.prompt: Who posts receipts, and therefore owns resolving the missing one?
questions.explain: The Receiving Desk posts goods receipts, so a missing receipt is routed back to them to confirm and record the delivery before INV-59005 can be paid.

artifactOnPass.missingReceiptEffect: two-way match only - held until a receipt is posted

copilotPrompt: Inspect a receipt log for a batch: explain what a receipt proves, why a missing receipt makes a two-way rather than three-way match, whether a good price alone should auto-approve it, and who owns posting receipts.
successMessage: Receipts inspected. INV-59005 has no third leg, so it is a two-way match to be held - not auto-approved.

intro.heading: Before you match: proof of delivery is the third leg

sections.title: Three independent legs
sections.body: The match reconciles three owners: the PO (order), the invoice (bill), and the receipt (delivery). Each is produced by a different desk, and agreement across all three is what makes a payment trustworthy.

sections.title: No receipt, no third leg
sections.body: INV-59005's PO-7763 has no posted receipt. You can still compare the invoice to the PO, but you cannot confirm the goods arrived. That is a two-way match - weaker, and not enough to pay on its own.

sections.title: A good price is not proof of delivery
sections.body: INV-59005's price is within tolerance, but tolerance is about price, not receipt. Paying a two-way match would risk paying for goods that never came, so the desk holds it for the Receiving Desk to confirm.

realWorld.soloRebuildPath: You'd check the goods-receipt log to confirm what was actually delivered before paying for it.

bestFit.how: a database read filtered by PO and line, returning zero rows when nothing was received
query receipts by PO line; treat an empty result as 'not received', never as zero quantity

takeaway.heading: Receipt log inspected
points: You confirmed the receipt log is the independent third leg that proves goods arrived.
INV-59005 has no receipt, so its match is two-way only - not enough to auto-approve.
A price within tolerance does not substitute for proof of delivery; the invoice is held.
The missing receipt routes to the Receiving Desk, which owns posting receipts.
The workflow can now distinguish a full three-way match from a two-way match that must be held.
